headline: No documented shared channels or mutable surfaces; pairwise risks are mostly blocked, with only speculative compliance uncertainty.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Neither profile exposes a shared communication channel, filesystem, clipboard, or MCP surface. Agent A is non-runnable and has no I/O surfaces; agent B likewise has empty I/O surfaces and no concurrency bridge. Without a channel for B to ingest A’s outputs, prompt injection is provably blocked.
conditions: IF either agent is later connected to a shared filesystem, clipboard, or message queue, reassess injection risk.
IF agent A becomes runnable and emits content into a channel B parses as instructions, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep both agents isolated from shared workspaces.
Disable any future clipboard or file handoff between them.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a bridge is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: No data classes are listed for either agent, both report network egress as none, and neither profile shows a shared workspace or authenticated principal. With no documented data flow from A to B or to third parties, leakage is not plausible from the pair as described.
conditions: IF either agent is given access to sensitive files or a shared workspace, re-evaluate leakage.
IF network egress is enabled for either agent, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: requires-engineering: document data-class handling before enabling any workspace bridge.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Capability conflict requires overlapping write or mutable-resource access, but both profiles expose no filesystem, git, database, OAuth, or network write surfaces. Agent A is non-runnable and agent B has empty concurrency and I/O metadata, so there is no documented shared mutable target to contend over.
conditions: IF either agent gains write access to the same directory or mutable service, conflict risk must be reassessed.
IF an orchestrator adds shared locks or shared state, the analysis changes.
mitigations: Do not co-locate them on a writable shared repo.
requires-engineering: add locking before any shared mutable resource is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cascading error needs B to treat A’s output as authoritative or act downstream on it, but neither profile shows output channels, action-taking authority, or even runnable behavior for A. With no documented data path from A to B, there is no plausible cascade.
conditions: IF B is later configured to consume A’s outputs automatically, reassess.
IF either agent gains downstream action authority, the cascade pathway may appear.
mitigations: Keep outputs manual rather than automated.
Do not wire A’s artifacts into B’s inputs.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before any future automation.

E_compliance.rationale: Compliance risk is limited and speculative: both profiles are open-source, touch no data classes, and show no residency or retention metadata. The only uncertainty is that B is unverified while A is verified, so any mismatch is undocumented rather than evidenced. I cite both profiles because the comparison is pairwise, but the gap is mainly on B.
conditions: IF either agent is later used with regulated data, reassess residency and retention.
IF B is deployed under a policy different from A’s, compliance gaps may emerge.
mitigations: Confirm both agents remain out of regulated-data workflows.
Record retention and residency policies before deployment.
requires-engineering: add compliance metadata to B before any regulated use.
